step1_figure.description: A standard CMOS inverter consisting of a PMOS pull-up transistor and an NMOS pull-down transistor, driving a capacitive load. It is the fundamental building block for digital logic and can also be analyzed as a simple high-gain analog amplifier.

switching_threshold.description: The input voltage (VSP) at which the input equals the output (Vin = Vout), causing both transistors to be in saturation.

equation.formula: V_SP = (V_DD - |V_THP| + V_THN * sqrt(beta_n / beta_p)) / (1 + sqrt(beta_n / beta_p))
equation.explanation: Derived by equating the saturation currents of the NMOS and PMOS transistors.
equation.assumptions: Assumes both devices are in strong inversion saturation and channel-length modulation is negligible.

sky130_expected.reasoning: The threshold is slightly skewed below VDD/2 (0.9V) because the NMOS is significantly stronger than the PMOS even with a 2:1 sizing ratio due to the high electron mobility in SKY130.

dc_gain.description: The small-signal voltage gain of the inverter when biased at its switching threshold.

equation.explanation: The ratio of total transconductance to total output conductance when both devices act as current sources.
equation.assumptions: Biased exactly at VSP; both devices in saturation.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Gain is limited by the channel length modulation (lambda=0.1/V) of short-channel devices.

propagation_delay.description: The time required for the output to cross 50% of VDD after the input crosses 50% of VDD.

equation.explanation: Approximates the discharge of the load capacitor by the average saturation current of the NMOS.
equation.assumptions: Input is an ideal step function; load is purely capacitive.

sky130_expected.reasoning: With a very small 10fF load and strong 1.8V drive, the intrinsic delay is extremely short, dominated by the high saturation current.

dynamic_power.description: Power dissipated by charging and discharging the load capacitance during switching.

equation.explanation: Energy per cycle is C*V^2, multiplied by the switching frequency.
equation.assumptions: Full rail-to-rail swing; short-circuit power is negligible.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming a switching frequency of 250 MHz (4ns period). P_dyn = 250e6 * 10e-15 * (1.8)^2 = 2.5e8 * 10e-15 * 3.24 = 8.1 uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Directly proportional to frequency and load capacitance. 8.1uW is expected for a 10fF load at 250MHz.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure the switching threshold, maximum DC gain, propagation delays, rise/fall times, and dynamic power of the SKY130 inverter.
step3_testbench.spice:
* SKY130 Inverter Characterization Testbench
.lib ${SKY130_PDK} tt
.option scale=1e-6
.option warn=0

* Define parameters for the parameterized netlist
.param W_x1=2 L_x1=0.15
.param W_x2=1 L_x2=0.15

* DUT Subcircuit
.subckt SKY130_INV OUT IN VSS VDD
x1 OUT IN VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_x1} l={L_x1}
x2 OUT IN VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_x2} l={L_x2}
.ends SKY130_INV

* Sources and Load
Vdd VDD 0 DC 1.8
Vss VSS 0 DC 0
Vin IN 0 DC 0.9 PULSE(0 1.8 1n 50p 50p 1n 2n)
Xinv OUT IN VSS VDD SKY130_INV
Cout OUT 0 10e-15

.control
* 1. DC Sweep Analysis for Switching Threshold and Gain
dc Vin 0 1.8 0.01
meas dc vsp when v(out)=0.9
let gain = deriv(v(out))
meas dc max_gain min gain

* 2. Transient Analysis for Delay and Power
tran 5p 4n
meas tran tphl trig v(in) val=0.9 rise=1 targ v(out) val=0.9 fall=1
meas tran tplh trig v(in) val=0.9 fall=1 targ v(out) val=0.9 rise=1
meas tran trise trig v(out) val=0.36 rise=1 targ v(out) val=1.44 rise=1
meas tran tfall trig v(out) val=1.44 fall=1 targ v(out) val=0.36 fall=1

* Measure average current from VDD to calculate power
meas tran avg_current avg i(Vdd)
let power = -avg_current * 1.8
print power

quit
.endc
.end
